why.title: A website that brings in clients, not one that only looks good
why.text: I build websites, landing pages and online shops for small and medium-sized businesses with custom code, without templates or page-builder plugins. That is what makes your site fast, secure and easy to find, and lets it do exactly what your business needs.

speed.title: Measurably fast

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about getting a website

items.q: How much does a website cost?
items.a: The price depends on the size of the job: a one-page landing page, a multi-page business website and an online shop are different tasks. You can find the current package prices on the services page, and an exact amount in a custom quote based on your needs.

items.q: How is custom development different from a template website?
items.a: Template sites made with a page builder load a lot of unnecessary code, so they are often slow and hard to extend. A custom site contains only what you need: it is faster, more secure, and can be extended with new features later.

Operation and maintenance are part of every project, from {{maintenance}} per month: servers, database, security updates and technical monitoring. You can still update the content yourself at any time.

items.q: Can we work together from anywhere?
items.a: Yes. The whole process can be done online by video call and e-mail, so I take on work from anywhere in Hungary, from Austria and beyond. In and around Sopron I am happy to meet in person too.

items.q: Can you also manage ads for the new site?
items.a: Yes. As a Google Ads Search certified developer I set up and manage Google Search ads, so the website and the campaign come from one hand and work together.

about.label: About
about.heading: Hi, I'm Szilveszter!
about.intro: I have been working in web development for two years now, and the code I write has already proven itself in the real world: my sites perform well in Google Search and reach outstanding scores in Google's official measurements (Lighthouse, PageSpeed Insights). That's why I can build websites that stay competitive even in the most saturated market segments.
about.introStrong: In practice, this means your website will not be a template-based, sluggish system, but a lightning-fast, secure, future-proof platform that also loads instantly on mobile.

custom.title: Custom
custom.text: Not a template, but a solution tailored to you.

accordion.title: What do you get from working with me?

items.title: What does a great website really do?
items.content: A great website is not just a digital business card and it is not only about looking nice. A professional site brings real clients, pre-qualifies leads for you, presents your references, and keeps your business available 24/7 without your phone having to ring all day. It automates your processes and builds trust in future clients before you even speak in person.

items.title: How am I different from template solutions?
items.content: While many websites on the market are built on heavy, stacked WordPress templates and unstable plugins, I work with fully custom code. For you, this means full design freedom, maximum data security, and outstanding load speed that Google rewards with better rankings.

items.title: Easy admin interface - hard to break
items.content: Forget overcomplicated and confusing dashboards. You get a clean admin interface tailored to you and your business, where you can edit text, upload new images, or update pricing in seconds, even from your phone. I structure it so the visual layout cannot be accidentally broken.

items.title: Visibility and Google rankings (Technical SEO)
items.content: Even the best website is useless if potential clients cannot find it. From the very first line of code, I focus heavily on SEO. Thanks to precise technical setup, custom metadata, and modern structure, your site starts with a technical advantage over local competitors.

items.title: Full-service delivery from planning to launch
items.content: I do not disappear after coding is done. Our collaboration covers the full process: concept planning, modern UI/UX design, high-performance development, optimized content setup, secure hosting and domain support, and connecting your site to Google services.

cards.title: Agile and transparent workflow
cards.content: I work with an agile mindset where continuous and honest communication is key. You always see where things stand, and the final result matches your expectations.

cards.title: Built for local businesses
cards.content: SynelWeb builds websites that are clear, fast, and easy to use. My goal is to make your website genuinely useful in day-to-day operations and easy for visitors to navigate.

cards.title: Sopron roots, nationwide reach
cards.content: I started out in Sopron, so I understand what local businesses need — but today I work just as effectively with clients across Hungary over online calls. The sites I build are flawless on mobile and give you a stable, long-term foundation, wherever you are.

cards.title: Personal and online support
cards.content: During development I am available both in person and online. The goal is a website that is not overcomplicated or overexplained, but simply works effectively.

cta.title: Let's kick off your business's digital growth!
cta.text: Let's level up and outrun your competitors with a website your visitors and Google will love. We can discuss your goals in an online session, or in person if you're near Sopron.

technology.label: Technology and quality
technology.heading: I build premium quality under the hood too.
technology.intro: Many people can create visually attractive websites, but the technical foundation often stays weak, slow, and hard to maintain. Here, the polished surface is backed by a stable system built for real business use.
technology.introStrong: I strongly believe outstanding design and premium engineering should always go hand in hand. I do not build from templates, but from modern technologies that create a fast, secure, and future-ready digital presence.
technology.beliefTitle: No-compromise design and engineering working together.
technology.beliefText: The goal is not just a beautiful website, but a system that loads quickly, scales cleanly, stays secure, and remains dependable for years. That is what turns a website into a real business asset.
technology.stackTitle: I do not rely on templates. I build with top-tier technologies.
technology.stackIntro: The technologies below ensure your website does not only look modern, but also delivers maximum value from both a technical and business perspective.

cards.name: React
cards.title: A lightning-fast and fluid user experience
cards.summary: React is the world's most popular modern UI technology, updating content instantly and app-like without disruptive full page reloads.
cards.valueLabel: What does this mean for your business?
cards.valueText: Your website feels faster and more premium to use, visitors are less likely to drop off while waiting, and they are more likely to stay engaged and reach out.

cards.name: TailwindCSS
cards.title: No-compromise custom design and speed
cards.summary: TailwindCSS makes it possible to craft a fully custom, pixel-precise and modern visual identity without dragging along heavy styling systems that slow the site down.
cards.valueLabel: What does this mean for your business?
cards.valueText: You get a visual style tailored to your business together with lightning-fast loading. No unnecessary code bloat, just a clean, lightweight and premium experience that both Google and visitors appreciate.

cards.name: TypeScript
cards.title: Rock-solid and intelligent code
cards.summary: TypeScript sits in the elite tier of modern web development: it catches hidden issues during development and leads to a clean, maintainable codebase.
cards.valueLabel: What does this mean for your business?
cards.valueText: Your site becomes more stable, easier to expand, and far less likely to fail unexpectedly, while giving your business a technical foundation that can grow with it.

cards.name: Python
cards.title: A future-ready and intelligent engine
cards.summary: Python is one of the world's most versatile programming languages, trusted by major technology platforms and modern AI systems alike.
cards.valueLabel: What does this mean for your business?
cards.valueText: You get a powerful backend with clean logic, ready for more complex business workflows, automations, and future expansion without unnecessary friction.

cards.name: Django Framework
cards.title: A hardened digital fortress
cards.summary: Django is a premium framework designed for secure, fast, and scalable server-side applications with battle-tested protections built in.
cards.valueLabel: What does this mean for your business?
cards.valueText: Your data and your clients' data stay strongly protected, while background processes run quickly, reliably, and almost invisibly to the end user.

cards.name: PostgreSQL
cards.title: An intelligent and precise database
cards.summary: PostgreSQL is one of the world's most advanced open-source databases, built to stay fast and accurate even under serious load.
cards.valueLabel: What does this mean for your business?
cards.valueText: Whether your site handles products, bookings, messages, or user data, it will continue serving visitors quickly and reliably even during heavier traffic.

technology.llmLabel: Why does this matter for AI-driven search?
technology.llmTitle: Algorithms can recognize technical quality too.
technology.llmText: When future clients ask AI systems for provider recommendations, those systems will evaluate not only the content, but also the technical quality behind a website. A modern, clean, and professional structure helps position you as a reliable expert at the front of the field.

proof.label: Proven results
proof.title: Not a promise, but measurable results
proof.intro: The code I write has already proven itself live: in search and in the official measurements. That's what matters when your website goes up against the competition.

search.title: Search
search.text: The sites I build perform well in Google's organic results, because their technical foundation – speed, clean structure, correct markup – is built for search engines from the start.

measured.title: Official measurements
measured.text: My sites are measured with Google's own tools, Lighthouse and PageSpeed Insights – and they consistently reach outstanding scores in performance, accessibility and SEO.

competitive.title: Even in saturated markets
competitive.text: Where many competitors fight for the same searches, technical quality decides. A site built this way stays competitive even in the most saturated market segments.

verifiable.title: Verifiable
verifiable.text: You don't have to take my word for it: the Lighthouse scores are shown next to every project in my references.

proof.valueTitle: What does this mean for your business?
proof.valueText: It means your website isn't backed by a slow, template-based system, but by a measurably fast foundation that competes in search – one that brings more visitors and doesn't collapse when traffic suddenly spikes.

cta.title: Let's build a website that feels premium inside and out.
cta.text: If design, performance, and long-term reliability all matter to you at once, then the technical foundation deserves the same level of attention as the visual layer.

cta.title: Want to fix what the check found?
cta.text: Speed, search visibility, technical setup: I'll go through your results with you, explain in plain words what matters most, and what fixing it – or a new site – would cost.

items.performance: How quickly the page loads and becomes usable – Google takes it into account for rankings.
items.accessibility: Whether everyone can use it: readable contrast, labels, keyboard navigation.
items.bestPractices: Security and modern techniques: HTTPS, error-free code, up-to-date image formats.
items.seo: The technical basics of SEO: titles, descriptions, indexability, mobile-friendly layout.
items.seoBasics: What Google's speed test doesn't cover: structured data, title and description, H1, indexability, sharing data, sitemap, robots.txt and llms.txt.
items.tech: The numbers behind loading: page weight, fonts, JavaScript and code splitting, caching, third parties, image and video formats.
items.platform: What the site is built with: a site builder or shop system (e.g. WordPress with Elementor, Wix, Shopify) or a custom build.

siteCheck.note: Scores are measured by Google PageSpeed Insights; the SEO basics and technical details are read by SynelWeb's own checker. Results can vary slightly between runs. We only store the address and the scores, no personal data.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
items: More than half of web traffic now comes from mobile devices – most of your visitors first meet your site on a phone.
Since 2023, Google uses the mobile version of a website for indexing and ranking. A slow mobile site is a disadvantage in search, too.
The mobile check simulates an average phone on a slower mobile connection, so mobile scores are usually lower than desktop ones – which is exactly why they deserve the most attention.

audit.seoText: What Google's speed test doesn't look at: what search engines and social networks read from your page.
audit.techText: The numbers behind loading: size, fonts, code, caching.

audit.clientRendered: The page's content is built in the browser with JavaScript, so not everything shows in its source code – and some search engines don't see it either.

structuredData.label: Structured data
structuredData.missing: No structured data: Google can't be sure who runs the site and shows no rich results (address, ratings, FAQ).
structuredData.noBusiness: Present ({{types}}), but the business details (Organization or LocalBusiness) are missing.
structuredData.invalid: {{invalid}} structured data block(s) are broken and can't be read by search engines.
structuredData.help: Hidden, machine-readable data in the page (business name, address, opening hours, FAQ). It tells Google who you are and powers rich results.

title.label: Page title
title.warn: {{length}} characters: 30–60 is ideal, otherwise Google cuts it or finds it too thin.
title.help: The title in the browser tab and the first line of the Google result – the first thing a searcher reads about you.

description.label: Meta description
description.fail: No meta description: Google picks a snippet itself.
description.help: The 1–2 sentence summary under the result. It doesn't rank directly, but it decides whether people click.

h1.label: H1 heading
h1.warn: {{count}} H1 headings; one main heading per page is clearest.
h1.help: The page's main heading. It's the quickest way for search engines to understand what the page is about.

indexable.label: Indexing
indexable.pass: Search engines may index the page.
indexable.fail: The page is blocked from search engines (noindex)!
indexable.help: A "noindex" tag keeps the page out of search results. Useful during development, a disaster when left on a live site.

canonical.label: Canonical URL
canonical.warn: Missing: if the content is reachable at several addresses, Google decides which one to show.
canonical.help: Tells search engines which address is the page's "original" when the same content is reachable at several (e.g. with and without www).

viewport.label: Mobile view
viewport.pass: The page is sized for mobile.
viewport.fail: No mobile viewport: phones show it zoomed out.
viewport.help: This setting lets the page fit the phone screen. Without it, phones show a tiny, zoomed-out page.

lang.label: Language
lang.help: Tells browsers and search engines the page's language, for correct translation, read-aloud and language-based results.

social.label: Sharing data
social.pass: Share title and image are set (Open Graph).
social.warn: Incomplete: on Facebook the link may show without an image or title.
social.help: Open Graph data decides which image and title appear when someone shares the link on Facebook or Messenger.

hreflang.label: Language versions
hreflang.info: None marked – fine for a single-language site.
hreflang.help: On a multilingual site it links the language versions, so everyone gets the result in their own language.

images.label: Image descriptions
images.pass: Every image has alt text ({{total}} images).
images.warn: {{missingAlt}} of {{total}} images have no alt text.
images.help: Alt text describes an image: screen readers read it aloud to blind users, and Google Images uses it to understand the picture.

https.label: HTTPS
https.fail: Not HTTPS: browsers mark it as "not secure".
https.help: The encrypted connection. Without it browsers show a warning and Google ranks the page lower.

robots.label: robots.txt
robots.fail: robots.txt blocks every search engine from the site!
robots.help: A small file telling search robots where they may go on the site. One wrong line can lock out the whole site.

sitemap.label: Sitemap
sitemap.warn: Not found: search engines discover the subpages more slowly.
sitemap.help: The site's table of contents for search engines: it lists every subpage so they get indexed faster and more completely.

video.label: Video formats
video.warn: Only {{formats}}: a WebM (VP9/AV1) version would be a fraction of the size, with an HEVC or MP4 fallback for Safari.
video.scripted: The source of {{count}} video(s) is added by JavaScript and can't be judged from the source code.
video.help: Modern video formats (WebM with VP9/AV1, or HEVC) are much smaller than classic MP4 (H.264) at the same quality. Best is to let the browser choose: WebM for Chrome and Android, HEVC or MP4 for Safari.

llmsTxt.label: llms.txt
llmsTxt.pass: llms.txt found: AI assistants quickly understand what the site is about.
llmsTxt.info: No llms.txt. New and optional, but it helps AI search tools like ChatGPT describe you accurately.
llmsTxt.help: llms.txt is a short Markdown description at the root of the site: who you are, what you offer and which pages matter most. AI search tools and assistants use it to understand the site faster and more accurately.

pageWeight.label: Page weight
pageWeight.warn: {{kb}} kB, {{requests}} requests – that already slows mobile connections.
pageWeight.fail: {{kb}} kB, {{requests}} requests – too heavy, slow on mobile.
pageWeight.help: All downloaded files together. The bigger it is, the longer it loads – especially on mobile data.

fonts.label: Fonts
fonts.warn: {{count}} font files ({{kb}} kB) – many: each is a separate download, or text shows late.
fonts.fail: {{count}} font files ({{kb}} kB) – too many fonts.
fonts.help: Every font and weight is a separate file. Many fonts slow loading and can make text "jump" as it appears.

javascript.label: JavaScript
javascript.warn: {{count}} files, {{kb}} kB, about {{unusedKb}} kB of it unused.
javascript.help: JavaScript makes a page interactive, but every kilobyte must be downloaded and run – phone processors feel it most.

codeSplitting.label: Code splitting
codeSplitting.pass: The largest script is {{largestKb}} kB – fine.
codeSplitting.warn: The largest script is {{largestKb}} kB: the code loads in one piece; splitting it per page would be faster.
codeSplitting.help: If a page loads all code at once, visitors download code the page doesn't use. Split up, each page loads only what it needs.

css.label: CSS
css.warn: {{count}} files, {{kb}} kB, about {{unusedKb}} kB of it unused.
css.help: CSS gives the page its look. Unused styles are extra downloads and delay the first render.

cache.label: Caching
cache.pass: Files can be cached for a long time.
cache.warn: {{shortCache}} files are cached only briefly: returning visitors download them again.
cache.help: Caching lets a returning visitor's browser skip downloading unchanged files. With short cache times every visit downloads them again.

domSize.label: Page structure (DOM)
domSize.warn: {{nodes}} elements – a large structure that slows rendering.
domSize.help: The number of building blocks on the page. With too many, the browser draws and updates the page more slowly.

thirdParty.label: Third parties
thirdParty.warn: {{count}} third-party services (trackers, chat widgets…) – each one slows the page.
thirdParty.help: Other companies' code on the page: analytics, ad pixels, chat widgets, embedded videos. Each is an extra download and extra waiting.

compression.label: Compression
compression.help: Text files (HTML, CSS, JS) shrink to a fraction of their size in transit when compressed. A server setting that costs visitors nothing.

imageFormats.label: Image formats
imageFormats.warn: Modern formats (WebP, AVIF) and compression would save about {{savingsKb}} kB.
imageFormats.help: Modern image formats (WebP, AVIF) are much smaller than JPG and PNG at the same quality.

platform.title: What is the site built with?
platform.unknown: Not recognisable – probably a custom build, or the traces are hidden.
platform.builderNote: Built with a site builder or template: quick to put together, but it usually loads a lot of unnecessary code that slows it down.
platform.customNote: A custom build loads only the code the site actually needs.
platform.disclaimer: Recognised from traces left in the page's source code.

trackers.label: Tracking
trackers.cookieless: Only cookieless measurement: {{cookieless}} – no consent needed.
trackers.help: Tracking scripts (e.g. Google Analytics, Meta Pixel) measure visitor behaviour and usually set cookies. In the EU they need the visitor's prior consent.

consent.label: Cookie consent
consent.pass: Cookie banner or Google Consent Mode found.
consent.notNeeded: No tracking that uses cookies, so no cookie banner is needed.
consent.warn: Embedded content (e.g. a map or video) sets cookies without consent – consider loading it on click.
consent.fail: {{tracking}} service(s) using cookies run, but no cookie banner was found: a GDPR risk.
consent.help: Under EU rules, cookies that aren't strictly necessary (analytics, ads) may only be set after the visitor agrees. That's what a cookie banner or consent tool is for.

privacyPolicy.label: Privacy notice
privacyPolicy.fail: No privacy notice found – required on almost every site (GDPR).
privacyPolicy.help: If a site handles any personal data (contact form, newsletter, analytics), the GDPR requires a clear notice: what, why, how long and on whose behalf.

imprint.label: Imprint
imprint.help: A business website must show the provider's details (name, address, contact, registration and tax number, host). In Austria the Impressum is particularly strict.

terms.label: Terms
terms.warn: Terms are required for an online shop, but none were found.
terms.info: No terms found – not necessarily required outside online shops.
terms.help: Terms set the conditions of buying or ordering (prices, delivery, withdrawal, warranty). Required for shops, strongly recommended for services.

cookiePolicy.label: Cookie policy
cookiePolicy.warn: The site runs services that use cookies, but no cookie policy was found.
cookiePolicy.info: No separate cookie policy – not needed without services that use cookies.
cookiePolicy.inPrivacy: No separate cookie notice. That's fine if the privacy notice lists the cookies the site uses.
cookiePolicy.help: A cookie policy lists which cookies the site uses, why and for how long. It can be part of the privacy notice.

audit.privacyText: Tracking, cookie consent and the required legal pages – from the source code.
audit.privacyDisclaimer: For information only, based on what the source code shows; not legal advice.
audit.shotsText: Snapshots of the loading: this is how long it takes for the content to appear.

siteCheck.h1: Free website check and speed test

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the website test

items.q: What counts as a good score?
items.a: Google treats 90–100 as good (green), 50–89 as needing improvement (orange) and below 50 as poor (red). Many template-based sites score far lower on mobile, so anything above 90 is outstanding.

items.q: Why is the mobile result worse than desktop?
items.a: The mobile test simulates a mid-range phone on a slower mobile connection, so the same page almost always scores lower on mobile. Since most visitors come from phones and Google uses the mobile version for ranking, the mobile result matters more.

Google's three measures of real user experience: when the largest content appears (LCP), how quickly the page responds to a click (INP), and how much the content jumps around while loading (CLS). Google also uses them for ranking.

The scores are measured by Google PageSpeed Insights, with the same Lighthouse Google uses. Results can differ by a few points between runs depending on the network and server at that moment, so it's worth testing more than once.

items.q: Do I need a cookie banner?
items.a: If the site uses a service that sets cookies – such as Google Analytics, Meta Pixel or an embedded map – EU rules require asking for the visitor's consent first. With only cookieless measurement, no banner is needed. The checker shows what runs on your site.

items.q: Is it free? What do you store?
items.a: Yes, it's free and needs no sign-up. We only store the address and the scores, no personal data. You can download the result as a PDF or attach it to a quote request.
